critical_code_review_comments: reels.tsx refactor is textbook expo-video: useEvent hook subscribes to statusChange, useEffect gates player.play() strictly on status === 'readyToPlay'. Removing .play() from the initializer eliminates the iOS race where the source hadn't been decoded yet — this is the recommended pattern.

Nice defensive touches: try/catch around play/pause with console.warn tagged by reel.id; error status logs raw error payload for on-device debugging. muted=true at init means iOS autoplay works without user-gesture, then unmuted only once the reel is active (line 76) — matches TikTok/Reels UX.
Three overlay states (paused/loading/error) now give the user visible feedback instead of a black frame, which was the underlying symptom of 'not playing'.

Backend purge_legacy_seed_data() is idempotent (runs on every startup, no-ops when clean) — safe for production. The 3-account cleanup during this iteration's restart is logged with count for auditability.
Cloudinary H.264 rewrite from iteration 9 is intact and still validated end-to-end (HEAD → codecs=avc1).

The 2 iteration-8 failures inside a mixed pytest run are a pre-existing ordering issue documented in iteration 9 — not introduced this iteration. Running iteration-8 in isolation (or after a backend restart) yields 6/6 pass.

rca_of_issue: Bug 1 root cause (iteration 10): expo-video's `useVideoPlayer` runs its initializer callback synchronously the first render, but the video source is loaded asynchronously. Calling `player.play()` inside the initializer means the play command hits the player BEFORE it transitions to `readyToPlay` status. On iOS specifically, this is either silently dropped or throws an internal AVPlayer error that expo-video swallows. The user sees a black screen and reports 'videos not playing'. Fix: subscribe to `statusChange` via useEvent, and only call `player.play()` in a useEffect that fires when status === 'readyToPlay' AND the reel is the active viewable item. This is the recommended expo-video pattern and is deterministic across iOS/Android/web. Combined with the iteration-9 backend H.264 rewrite (which was the codec-side of the problem), reels should now play on all supported devices. Bug 2 (iteration 10): purely operational — testing agents from prior iterations left behind 3 tec_*/tpb_* scratch users. The startup purge in `purge_legacy_seed_data()` is idempotent and was triggered by the backend restart; DB now contains exactly one user (`semidiepie`) confirmed via /api/admin/users.
